parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: An electron is initially at the energy level $-0.85\text{ eV}$. State the total number of different wavelengths that may be emitted as the electron de-excites (loses energy).

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
(c)(ii) Photons resulting from electron de-excitation from the $-0.85\text{ eV}$ energy level are incident on the surface of a sample of platinum.

Platinum has a work function energy of $5.6\text{ eV}$.

Determine

1. the maximum kinetic energy, in $\text{eV}$, of a photoelectron emitted from the surface of the platinum,

2. the wavelength of the photon producing the photoelectron in (ii) part 1.
